note: Benchmaxxing calibration tier table (job bh-benchmaxxing-calibration-20260917). Keyed by benchmark family (registry id before '::'). Tiers: headline = public question set that labs quote in release posts, so it is the board most exposed to targeted tuning and contamination; heldout = private/unpublished questions, tasks created after most training cutoffs, or a held-out split, which a lab cannot tune toward; domain = a vertical professional domain (legal, finance, spreadsheet, medical) whose gaps mostly show specialisation; secondary = public but rarely quoted, or measures a trait rather than task skill; aggregate = an index built from other boards (never compared); judged = graded by votes or a judge model (already outside the signal). Only benchmark facts decide a tier, never who scores well on it. 2026-09-19 (CR-54.2): six Epoch AI Benchmarking Hub boards joined with deliberate tiers; math_level_5 (2021 legacy, saturated MATH-500 precedent) and frontiermath_erdos (all five published rows score 0, not in ECI, benchmark_metadata leaves its source file blank) were excluded — see data/raw/benchmarks/epoch-hub-decisions.json.

aa-aime.reason: AIME 2025 problems are public and quoted in nearly every reasoning-model release post.

aa-gpqa-diamond.reason: Public 198-question set, the most-quoted science number in release posts.

openrouter-gpqa-diamond.reason: Same public GPQA Diamond questions, re-run by OpenRouter.

aa-hle.reason: Humanity's Last Exam questions are public and a standard release-post headline.

aa-scicode.reason: Public SciCode problems, long part of the widely quoted AA index.

aa-ifbench.reason: Public IFBench prompts and checkers, quoted in open-model cards.

aa-tau2-telecom.reason: tau2-bench is public and one of the most-quoted agent numbers in release posts.

openrouter-tau2-bench-airline.reason: Public tau2-bench airline domain, re-run by OpenRouter.

aa-terminal-bench.reason: Terminal-Bench 2.x tasks are public and quoted in nearly every coding/agent release post.

vals-index-terminal-bench-2.1.reason: Same public Terminal-Bench 2.1 tasks, run by Vals.

aa-terminal-bench-hard.reason: Pinned subset of the public Terminal-Bench tasks.

aa-mmmu-pro.reason: Public MMMU-Pro questions, the standard vision headline.

aa-lcr.reason: AA-LCR dataset is published and quoted in open-model cards.

simpleqa-verified.reason: Public SimpleQA Verified questions, quoted in release posts.

aa-omniscience.reason: Private AA question set; also penalises confident wrong answers, which tuning on public sets does not help.

aa-critpt.reason: Research-level physics with answers kept private by the authors.

aa-tau3-banking.reason: New tau3 banking domain, not yet a release-post number.

aa-automationbench.reason: AA runs a held-out split of AutomationBench.

aa-enterpriseops-gym.reason: New enterprise MCP environments, not a release-post number.

aa-itbench.reason: AA's offline incident snapshots, not quoted by labs.

aa-terminal-bench@4.0.reason: Terminal-Bench v4.0 is a fresh task set released after most current models were trained; applies to version 4.0 only.

aa-terminal-bench@4.0-upstream-timeouts.reason: The same fresh Terminal-Bench v4.0 task set under AA's 2026-09-21 harness configuration (tasks' own timeouts); applies to this version only.

deepswe.reason: Original long-horizon tasks written by Datacurve, not public repos' history.

frontiermath-tiers-1-3.reason: Unpublished problems, run only by Epoch AI.

frontiermath-tier-4.reason: Unpublished research-level problems, run only by Epoch AI.

matharena-arxivmath.reason: Problems from June 2026 arXiv papers, newer than training data.

vals-index-code-migration.reason: Vals private task set (general coding, not a vertical domain).

vals-index-finance-agent.reason: Vertical finance work; a gap shows specialisation.

gso.reason: Public repos, rarely quoted; tiny cohort (10).

bullshitbench-v1.reason: Measures a trait (premise pushback), not task skill.

bullshitbench-v2.reason: Measures a trait (premise pushback), not task skill.

aa_coding_index.reason: Average of AA coding component boards.

vals-index.reason: GDP-weighted average of its Vals component boards.

aa-apex-agents.reason: Graded deliverables (judge); already outside the signal.

aa_agentic_index.reason: Average of Artificial Analysis' agentic evaluations (one measured configuration per model), relayed by OpenRouter's Benchmarks API.

weirdml.reason: Hand-made, newly published tasks (WeirdML v3, September 2026), not part of any public training-ready question set.

vulcanbench-frontier.reason: Public open-source task suites (v4-suite GitHub org) behind hidden tests; rarely quoted in launch posts; 33% of the combined score is judge-graded code quality.

kernelbench-cuda-glm52-fused-moe.reason: Public CUDA problems with public reference solutions in the maintainer’s GitHub monorepo; rarely quoted in launch posts.

kernelbench-cuda-deepseek-nsa.reason: Public CUDA problems with public reference solutions in the maintainer’s GitHub monorepo; rarely quoted in launch posts.

kernelbench-cuda-megaqwen-decode.reason: Public CUDA problems with public reference solutions in the maintainer’s GitHub monorepo; rarely quoted in launch posts.

kernelbench-cuda-grid-mingru-sps.reason: Public CUDA problems with public reference solutions in the maintainer’s GitHub monorepo; rarely quoted in launch posts.

chess-puzzles.reason: 100 novel chess positions generated programmatically by Epoch AI (published 2025-12-10) that “do not appear in any other source”; cannot be trained verbatim.

mystery-game-puzzles.reason: Epoch keeps the game's identity deliberately undisclosed and generates the puzzles programmatically (published 2026-07-30); benchmark-specific preparation is designed out.

ebr-bench.reason: Epoch chose the relatively obscure board game Earthborne Rangers precisely so models are unlikely to have memorised it; measures learning across repeated playthroughs (published 2026-07-01).

mirrorcode.reason: Whole-program reimplementation from publicly known programs with held-out tests, co-developed with METR (published 2026-06-26); rarely quoted in launch posts.

epoch-gpqa-diamond.reason: The same public GPQA Diamond questions the AA and OpenRouter runs use, re-run by Epoch AI; the most-quoted science number in release posts.

epoch-swe-bench-verified.reason: Public SWE-bench Verified tasks re-run by Epoch AI; the existing SWE-bench Verified board carries the same default tier, so the duplicate stays out of the headline/heldout pairs.

frontierswe.reason: Public task suite on GitHub (Proximal-Labs/frontier-swe-v2) behind the site’s own review protocol; rarely quoted in launch posts; the site itself is the only leaderboard for it.

posttrainbench.reason: Public retraining protocol and harness (aisa-group/PostTrainBench, MIT; arXiv2603.08640, verified by Epoch AI); a base-model retraining eval quoted on posttrainbench.com only.

rsi-exam.reason: Every task score comes from a sealed hidden split the agent never sees, 53 of the 88 tasks are held back entirely, and the tasks were written for this benchmark in 2026 by domain experts — a lab cannot tune toward the graded data.

toolathlon.reason: The original release's task set and evaluators are public in the maintainers' GitHub repository, and labs quoted it in release material before the Verified repair — the committed Lumina ledger (data/raw/lumina-ledger.json, family toolathlon) counts 15 vendor-reported results cited from Meta, DeepSeek, Google DeepMind, Kimi and Z.ai pages — so it was a board a training team could aim at.

toolathlon-verified.reason: Public task set and evaluators in the maintainers' GitHub repository, and our own self-reported corpus shows eight labs quoting Toolathlon in release material — 41 rows name the Verified series (e.g. Anthropic's Fable 5.1 system card) — so it is a board a training team can aim at.

livebench.reason: Public official leaderboard whose questions are not published as private or held back anywhere in our verified capture, and which no row of our self-reported corpus quotes (0 of 78 rows, against 41 for Toolathlon-Verified) — public but rarely quoted. The board's contamination-limiting refresh is not a fact our source states: the registry entry records "no promised publication schedule", and this release (2026-06-25) predates several models measured on it, so heldout is not claimed.

mcp-atlas.reason: Half public, half held out: the 500-task public subset is on Hugging Face with the harness on GitHub, the other 500 tasks are not, and Scale runs every row itself. Our self-reported corpus finds one lab quoting MCP-Atlas in release material (StepFun's Step 5 Preview), so it is a public board that is rarely quoted — neither heldout nor a board training teams broadly aim at.

context-arena-mrcr-v2.reason: Synthetic long-context retrieval task on Google DeepMind's public MRCR v2 dataset, run by one independent maintainer; it measures a context-length trait rather than task skill, and our self-reported corpus holds no MRCR row, so it is not evidenced as a board labs quote in release material.

blueprint-bench.reason: Andon Labs runs every model itself on 50 apartments whose photos and floor plans it does not say are public or private; the page states neither a public task set nor a held-out split, and our self-reported corpus holds no Blueprint-Bench row, so it is not evidenced as a board labs quote in release material.

long-horizon-terminal-bench.reason: The 46 task environments are public on Hugging Face (Apache-2.0) while the verifiers that grade them stay hidden, and the maintainers replay every submitted run themselves; the board is a lab's (Tencent HY) own report with its model Hy3 among the rows, and our self-reported corpus holds no Long-Horizon Terminal-Bench row, so it is not evidenced as a board labs quote in release material.

react-native-evals.reason: An LLM judge rules each written requirement met or not against the generated code; a judge's ruling, not a test or reference answer, is the score.

researchclawbench.reason: An LLM acting as a strict peer reviewer grades each research report against a weighted rubric; the judge's rating is the score.

matharena-hmmt.reason: HMMT's contest problems are public once the tournament is held, and labs quote HMMT in release material — our self-reported corpus (data/raw/benchmarks/self-reported/scout-20260915.jsonl.gz) holds HMMT February 2026 rows from DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, MBZUAI, Alibaba Qwen and Z.ai and HMMT November 2025 rows from Alibaba Qwen and Z.ai — so it is a board a training team can aim at.

matharena-apex.reason: MathArena publishes the twelve Apex problems on Hugging Face, and labs quote it in release material — our self-reported corpus holds MathArena Apex rows from DeepSeek and Nex AGI.

matharena-apex-shortlist.reason: MathArena publishes the 47 Apex Shortlist problems on Hugging Face, and labs quote it in release material — our self-reported corpus holds Apex Shortlist rows from DeepSeek and Motif Technologies.

matharena-aime.reason: AIME's contest problems are public once the exam is held (MathArena publishes the 30 AIME 2026 problems on Hugging Face), and labs quote AIME 2026 in release material — our self-reported corpus (data/raw/benchmarks/self-reported/scout-20260915.jsonl.gz) holds AIME 2026 rows from Moonshot AI (Kimi K2.6 card) and Z.ai (GLM-5.2 card) and, written "AIME26", from Alibaba Qwen (Qwen3.6-27B card) — so it is a board a training team can aim at.

matharena-usamo.reason: LLM judges grade each proof against a rubric that a model writes from the official solution (MathArena's configs/judges/main_judge.yaml and grading_scheme_creator.yaml); a judge's reading of the proof, not a checkable answer, sets the score, and three of the judge models are graded on the same board.
